situation: Paged at night for a database disk filling steadily, with no users affected yet.
decision: Find and reverse what is writing (lower log level or pause the job), avoid deleting files, and escalate only past a threshold.

moves.name: estimate time available before acting
moves.step: Work out how long until the failure lands to decide how fast you must move.
moves.cue: a resource filling at a steady rate
moves.evidence: I have roughly an hour and a half before it's full

moves.name: look at what changed, not the symptom
moves.step: Ask what started writing rather than examining the full disk.
moves.cue: a growing resource at an odd hour
moves.evidence: I'd look at what's writing, not at the disk.

moves.name: avoid the irreversible move at 2am
moves.step: Refuse actions you cannot undo when tired and under pressure; pause rather than kill.
moves.cue: temptation to delete files to buy space
moves.evidence: What I would not do at 2am is start deleting files on the primary

moves.name: size the escalation to who is affected
moves.step: Page more people only as the number affected or the threshold rises.
moves.evidence: So this is not a wake-everyone-up incident.

considerations.evidence: 2am is exactly when people make irreversible mistakes
